rationale: The massing reads as a nested bar composition around a central carved void, and that dominant idea is legible across the views. There is a clear main/support relationship, but the lower and upper bars feel slightly separated rather than fully integrated into one anchor mass. The silhouette is not purely stepback-driven, though some of the read depends on staggered plate shifts and thin bar projections. The void is meaningful but somewhat enclosed and internal, so its publicness is only moderate. Overall the form appears mostly coherent in multiple views, with some risk of clip-like segmentation and minor cross-view alignment ambiguity. It resonates with precedent principles of stacked platforms and atrium carving without directly copying any one reference.
warnings: Some planes read as thin, almost detached plates rather than one continuous mass.
The void is legible but not strongly opened to ground or public edge.
A few overhangs/offsets may be vulnerable to repair simplification if iterated further.
